subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should this remain the umbrella tracker for multi-agent orchestration stability while narrower fixes land, or should maintainers split the remaining work into canonical narrower issues?
rationale: Current main has partial fixes, but the remaining work spans strict bugs, session-state architecture, cancellation semantics, and completion-payload policy that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Narrow Fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open as the routing umbrella while reviewing linked repairs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540 and reassess after they land or close.

options.title: Split Canonical Remaining Work
options.body: Promote the active narrower issues as canonical, link this evidence there, and close the umbrella only after the split is explicit.

options.title: Sponsor Orchestration Redesign
options.body: Treat the token-ring or metadata-only completion direction as a product-design effort instead of a bug cleanup lane.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Narrow Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the routing umbrella while reviewing linked repairs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540 and reassess after they land or close.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest feature-history trail across the affected subagent/session-lock architecture and repository vision boundaries.
